youtube.title: Who discovered insulin, and where was it first injected? A $1 patent 💉
youtube.description:
London, Berlin or the third one? A century ago a dying teenager weighing 29 kg was given a cloudy extract from animal pancreases. The first shot failed; the second changed medicine forever. The men behind it sold the patent to their university for a single dollar.
Guess before the map lights up, then see the hospital, the blood-sugar drop, and the price of the patent.
Which did you pick? World Diabetes Day falls this week.

v04.text: Toronto. On 11 January 1922, at Toronto General Hospital, 14-year-old Leonard Thompson got the first injection.

v05.text: The first dose was impure. 12 days later a purified extract dropped his blood sugar to normal.

v06.text: Banting and Best had extracted it from dog pancreases the summer before, in a borrowed university lab.

research.topic: First insulin injection into a human: Leonard Thompson, 14, Toronto General Hospital, 11 January 1922 (impure extract, sterile abscess); purified extract by James Collip given 23 January 1922 lowered blood glucose from 0.52 % to 0.12 %; Banting and Best isolated the extract from dog pancreases in Macleod's lab, University of Toronto, summer 1921; patent assigned to the University of Toronto for $1; Nobel Prize 1923 to Banting and Macleod.

myths.myth: Insulin was a European discovery like most early-20th-century pharmacology.
myths.reality: It was isolated and first used clinically in Toronto, Canada, in 1921–22 by Banting, Best, Collip and Macleod.

landscape.our_gap: Feed clips name Banting as a one-liner; nobody pins the hospital, runs the blood-sugar counter from the 1922 case notes and wipes DEATH SENTENCE off the screen on a moving map.

nobel_insulin.title: The discovery of insulin
nobel_insulin.notes: Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1923 to Frederick Banting and John Macleod for the discovery of insulin; Toronto 1921–22

uoft_insulin100.title: Insulin 100 — the discovery of insulin
uoft_insulin100.notes: Banting and Best began experiments on dog pancreases in May 1921 in Macleod's lab; first human injection to Leonard Thompson, 14, at Toronto General Hospital on 11 January 1922; Collip's purified extract given 23 January 1922; patent sold to the University of Toronto for $1

britannica_insulin.title: Frederick Banting — Canadian physician
britannica_insulin.notes: with Charles Best isolated insulin in 1921 at the University of Toronto; first used on a 14-year-old diabetic boy in January 1922; Nobel Prize 1923

cmaj_1922.publisher: Canadian Medical Association Journal (via PubMed Central)
cmaj_1922.title: Pancreatic extracts in the treatment of diabetes mellitus — Banting, Best, Collip, Campbell, Fletcher, CMAJ 1922;12(3):141–146
cmaj_1922.notes: case of L.T., 14: first extract 11 January 1922 produced a sterile abscess and modest effect; purified extract from 23 January lowered blood sugar from 0.52 % to 0.12 % and cleared glycosuria

minkowski.title: Oskar Minkowski — German physician
minkowski.notes: with Joseph von Mering showed in 1889 that removing a dog's pancreas produces diabetes

diabetes_uk.title: The history of insulin
diabetes_uk.notes: before 1922 a type 1 diagnosis meant death within months to a couple of years on starvation diets; Banting sold the patent for $1 saying insulin belonged to the world
